bull_bear.body:
- Anchor-customer relationship: infrastructure facilities and support services are provided mainly to Reliance Industries Limited
- Conservative financial profile — the Company continues to maintain its conservative financial profile and funds its requirements through internal accruals
- Long-life pipeline infrastructure with cathodic-protection and SCADA-based real-time monitoring maintained under an obsolescence-management programme
- Management team with relevant experience and operational depth in infrastructure, supported by governance structures for oversight and accountability
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Operational disruption of pipeline operations, including third-party damage in high consequence areas — The AR flags that pipeline operations may be disrupted by natural calamities, equipment failures or unforeseen events, with third-party damage to pipelines in high consequence areas named as a key risk; mitigation relies on line patrolling, SOP adherence, stakeholder awareness, periodic inspections and external audits.
- Safety, health and environment hazards inherent in transporting petroleum products and natural gas — The AR states this transportation involves inherent hazards including accidents, leakages or external threats that may impact life, property and the environment; addressed through structured inspections, hazard identification, root cause analysis, preventive measures and comprehensive insurance cover.
- Customer concentration — services provided mainly to Reliance Industries Limited — The Company states it provides infrastructure facilities and support services mainly to Reliance Industries Limited, and Form AOC-2 records a single material arm's-length arrangement with RIL, its promoter, covering transportation and infrastructure support services. Revenue therefore depends on one counterparty and on continuation of those arrangements.
- Expiry / non-renewal of fixed-term contracts — Revenue from infrastructure support services and other operating income fell to ₹ 1,213 lakh from ₹ 1,632 lakh 'following the completion of certain fixed-term contracts', showing that contract expiry directly reduces the revenue base.
- Environmental assessment and sustainability compliance costs, with regulatory and reputational exposure — The MD&A states environmental assessments and sustainability compliance have become substantive cost items, and that regulatory and reputational considerations in this area represent material risk factors for the sector.
- Availability of skilled labour — Named in the MD&A 'Challenges, Risks and Concerns' as adding complexity to the overall business environment.
- Volatility in input costs — Named in the MD&A 'Challenges, Risks and Concerns' alongside skilled-labour availability; the MD&A also notes execution gaps and cost pressures persist in India's infrastructure sector.
- External environment — conflicts disrupting freight corridors and commodity markets — The MD&A records that ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and Eastern Europe continued to disrupt freight corridors and commodity markets with no clear resolution in sight, and that persistent supply chain disruptions continue.

- Keep governance structures and prudent financial management central to project delivery and operational continuity, with continuous evaluation of evolving risk factors

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Annual Report discloses no expansion project, capacity addition or commissioning timeline. The Company states it continues to provide the same infrastructure facilities and support services — pipelines for transportation of petroleum products, natural gas and raw water, and other infrastructure support services — mainly to Reliance Industries Limited, with no change in the nature of its business. Asset spend during the year was confined to obsolescence management and technology upgradation of existing assets: replacement of old battery banks at Cathodic Protection stations CP-3, CP-4, CP-5 and CP-6 with an energy-efficient power storage system, and upgradation of the 48V DC / 24V DC charger panel system and the SCADA interface panel at CP-5. The Company did not import any major technology during the last three years and incurred no research and development expenditure. There have been no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of the Report.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural demand for infrastructure in India remains intact, underpinned by India's long-term industrial expansion
- Government's continued prioritization of capital expenditure in roads, ports, pipelines and logistics has supported the broader momentum of infrastructure development in the country
- Persistent supply chain disruptions have prompted a broader rethink of import dependencies, strengthening the case for domestic infrastructure capacity
- Global environment remained challenging in FY 2025-26 — ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and Eastern Europe continued to disrupt freight corridors and commodity markets, with no clear resolution in sight
- India's infrastructure sector has held up reasonably well, though execution gaps and cost pressures persist
- Infrastructure support services revenue declined following the completion of certain fixed-term contracts, while transportation services revenue was broadly flat
